6. On an oral request of the petitioner, the other accused persons are allowed to be impleaded as petitioners.
7. The learned counsel for the petitioner has handed over the Amended Memo of Parties impleading all the accused as petitioners.
The same is taken on record.
He submits that the petitioner no.2 has since expired, therefore, the criminal proceedings against him stands abated.
The factum of death of petitioner no.2 is affirmed by the learned APP for State, on instructions from the I.O, who is present in court.

8. The petitioner no.1 (former husband) and petitioners nos. 3 and 4 who are close relatives of petitioner no.1, as well as, respondent no. 2 (former wife) are present in the court and they have been identified by their respective counsels and by the Insp. Abhishek Singh and ASI Babu Lal, PS.
Vijay Vihar.
9. The brief facts of the case are that the marriage between the parties was solemnized on 14.10.2018 according to Hindu Rites and Ceremonies.
No child was born out of the said wedlock.
10. On account of temperamental issues, certain disputes arose between the parties and they started living separately w.e.f. 21.04.2019.
The dispute This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/09/2023 at 19:29:30 between the parties also led to the registration of present FIR.

11. During the pendency of the proceedings, the parties were referred to the Delhi Mediation Centre,
Rohini Courts, where they arrived at a settlement, terms whereof were reduced in writing in the form of a Settlement/Agreement dated 20.07.2022, which is annexed as Annexure P-4 to the petition.
12. In terms of the said settlement the parties have decided to dissolve their marriage by decree of divorce by mutual consent.
Accordingly, the parties have obtained a decree of divorce dated 09.06.2023, which is annexed as Annexure P-3 to the petition.

13. It is also a term of the said settlement that the petitioner no.1 shall pay a total sum of Rs.1.90 lacs to the respondent no.2 towards full and final settlement of all her claims on account of maintenance (past, present and future), permanent alimony, stree dhan and dowry articles.

Out of the said amount, a sum of Rs. 1.5 lacs has already been paid in the manner as mentioned in the settlement by the petitioner no.1 to the respondent no.2, the receipt of which respondent no.2 acknowledges.

The remaining amount of Rs.40,000/- has been paid to the respondent no.2 by the petitioner no.1 today in the court by way of Demand Draft bearing no.258006 dated 18.07.2023 issued by the Sarva Haryana Gramin Bank, Budhpur, Rewari, in favour of respondent no.2/Sudha.
14.
The respondent no.2, who is present in Court, acknowledges having received the entire amount of Rs. 1.90 lacs.

On a query made by this court, the respondent no.2 states that she has no objection, in case the aforesaid FIR is quashed.
16. In view of the fact that the parties have amicably resolved their This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/09/2023 at 19:29:30 disputes out of their own free will and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
17. It is thus in the interest of justice that the present FIR and all the other proceedings emanating therefrom be quashed.

18. Consequently, the petition is allowed and FIR No. 285/2019 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at Police Station Vijay Vihar is quashed along with all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
19. The petition stands disposed off, in the above terms.
20. Order be uploaded on the website of this court.
